notes.text: Clayton Vernon sent Vince Kaminski and Vasant Shanbhogue a summary of his meeting with Chris Germany, Capacity Trader at the East Desk, on gas transmission pricing.

Per Germany, pipeline capacity is typically leased monthly. Example South Texas to Brooklyn: about $12.00 per month per 10,000 decatherms (about $0.40/day), plus variable charges of 6% fuel (shrinkage) and 6.5% overhead.

Trader spread example: South Texas delivered at NYMEX minus $0.10 basis, Brooklyn at NYMEX plus $0.25, spread $0.35. With variable transmission cost $0.125, a trader could offer up to $0.225 for firm capacity for tomorrow.

Germany said leaseholders know the firm equivalent of interruptible capacity well, and many pipelines don't discount firm tariff maximums. Several physical routes exist (Enron, Texas Eastern, etc.); traders cover pipeline positions at each end to free capacity.

notes.text: John Sherriff (Enron Europe, 7 Dec 1999 announcement) announced the formation of the Credit Markets Group, which develops products to manage Enron's internal credit portfolio risk and offers third-party credit protection.
The Credit Markets Group will initially make markets in bankruptcy protection on reference credits in Enron's current portfolio, with more credit products and reference credits expected soon.

The Credit Markets Group plans to use EnronOnline as its primary trade execution tool and to launch an external credit protection website with real-time prices, filtering by reference credit, credit models and research papers. A public announcement is expected in late January.
The Credit Markets Group will be based in London, with an initial local desk in Houston.
Bryan Seyfried is transitioning out of RAC (where he ran the European Trading Controls and Research teams) to lead the Credit Markets Group, reporting to John Sherriff.
